thought.text: Token validity has been conclusively confirmed: no token → 401, invalid token → 401, `.env.local` token → 200. The hash comparison was my artifact (Laravel hashes the tokens). Next, I'll test the actual login flow to the Filament admin panel and web app, and after that, run the backend test suite to confirm that the development environment is functioning correctly.

reasoning_content:
The token hash issue has been resolved: Laravel's `personal_access_tokens.token` column is hashed, but the 200 response from the live authenticated call against a 401 response with no/invalid token is conclusive proof that the stored token is valid and working. The sha256 "mismatch" was an artifact of my own computation (Laravel may be hashing differently — in fact, the stored value has the format of a bcrypt/argon hash, but it's shown as hex... in any case, the behavioral evidence is decisive: no auth → 401, invalid auth → 401, valid auth → 200).

Now, let me do a few final checks:
1. Filament login on port 3001 — I've confirmed that the login form renders. I could also try an actual login, but that requires CSRF handling. Let me try it to get the strongest evidence.
2. Login to the Web frontend on port 3000.
3. Swagger UI content (title already confirmed, and the spec has been loaded).
4. Backend PHPUnit tests — the guide says `php artisan test`. Running the entire test suite may be optional, but it would be good evidence of the development environment. It might take a while, so let me run it with a timeout.

Let me try Filament's actual login flow and the web app's login flow. For Filament:
- GET /admin/login → obtain XSRF-TOKEN cookie
- POST /admin/login with the csrf token

Let me run this with curl using a cookie jar.

action.command:
echo "=== Filament admin panel login test (hello@vereinfacht.digital) ==="
cd /tmp && rm -f cj.txt
# Get CSRF token
CSRF=$(curl -s -c cj.txt --max-time 15 http://localhost:3001/admin/login | grep -oP 'name="_token" value="\K[^"]+' | head -1)
echo "CSRF obtained: ${CSRF:+yes}"
# Submit login
curl -s -b cj.txt -c cj.txt --max-time 20 -o /tmp/login_resp.html -w "Login POST: HTTP %{http_code} -> %{redirect_url}\n" \
  -X POST http://localhost:3001/admin/login \
  -H "X-CSRF-TOKEN: $CSRF" \
  --data-urlencode "_token=$CSRF" \
  --data-urlencode "email=hello@vereinfacht.digital" \
  --data-urlencode "password=password"
# Check we can now access authenticated page
curl -s -b cj.txt --max-time 20 http://localhost:3001/admin -o /tmp/admin_dash.html -w "GET /admin (authed): HTTP %{http_code} -> %{redirect_url}\n"
grep -oiE 'Filament|dashboard|<title>[^<]*' /tmp/admin_dash.html | sort -u | head -8
